candidates.rationale: ROE that co-moves with rising leverage is debt-fueled rather than organic profitability (a DuPont quality-of-earnings read); low co-movement should predict higher forward returns.
The fraction of the trailing four quarters with conservative, income-decreasing accruals is a persistence-weighted earnings-quality score, sturdier than a single quarter's accrual reading.
Book cheapness priced consistently against raw $open (book_per_share is raw-scale, unlike adjusted $close) net of leverage instability isolates safe value from balance-sheet value traps.
Earnings-yield cheapness (again $open-anchored to keep both legs on the raw price scale) combined with low trading activity targets mispricing that persists longest where arbitrage is costliest.
High-margin firms whose intraday trading range is genuinely widening over the past quarter are more likely being re-rated on real information than low-margin firms showing the same range expansion.

Quality showing up through either strong margins or strong asset returns (not requiring both at once) net of leverage risk avoids penalizing firms whose quality channel is narrower than a multiplicative composite assumes.

Margin quality ranked against a leverage change sized relative to the firm's own base (not the raw point change) isolates margin-led improvement from leverage swings that scale very differently for low- vs high-debt firms.
Conservative accruals paired with low realized return volatility identify the 'boring, high quality-of-earnings' cohort, a quality-conditioned low-volatility tilt distinct from either effect alone.

Highly levered firms' short-term price swings are more likely pure liquidity-driven overreaction than fundamentals-driven, so a leverage-conditioned 5-day reversal should mean-revert more reliably than an unconditional one.

The Sharpe ratio of quarter-over-quarter EPS changes rewards firms whose earnings grow steadily over firms delivering the same average growth erratically, a quality-of-growth signal distinct from the growth level itself.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.

Working memory: rules written after earlier rounds on this island, oldest first. Apply them.
  1. Favor more variations on value x quality products (a book/price-style ratio times a profitability rank) — this shape scored 8.954 this round, far above every other accept and above the quality-momentum and quality-leverage spreads that also cleared.
  2. Avoid CS_ZSCORE(return-or-volume ratio) multiplied against a single fundamental rank — this combination scored |t| 0.02 and 0.59 in two attempts this round, well under the CS_RANK*CS_RANK product/spread shapes that were accepted.
  3. Delta the raw fundamental before ranking it, not after — TS_DELTA(CS_RANK($roe), 21) scored |t| 0.26, far weaker than the accepted CS_RANK($roe) - CS_RANK(TS_MEAN($return, 63)) spread built from the same field.
  4. Check within-run duplicates more carefully around $open/$high/$low extremum ratios sharing a window — 3 of this round's 20 rejects were exact repeats already proposed earlier in the same run.
  5. A single swapped leaf (one OHLC field for another, or which field sits in numerator vs denominator) inside an otherwise-archived multi-term shape still shares 4-6 nodes and trips archive_subtree — vary an inner operator or restructure the term, not just the leaf.
  6. $asset_turnover was the common leg in both bare fundamental-difference cheap_screen fails this round (CS_RANK(-$accrual_gap)-CS_RANK($asset_turnover) at |t| 0.21; CS_RANK($asset_turnover)-CS_RANK($roe) at |t| 0.72), while operating_margin-leverage passed as a bare difference in the same round — treat $asset_turnover as a weak bare spread leg regardless of partner, not just a bad pairing.
  7. CS_RANK(TS_DELTA($leverage,126)) - CS_RANK($roe) is now saturated against any dressing of the leverage leg: multiplying by TS_RANK(dollar_volume) or TS_RANK(return), or dividing by $close, all landed rho 0.97-0.99 this round (3 rejects). The same leverage-delta term times a volume rank still accepts fine standalone (fitness 0.507) — it's pairing against $roe specifically that's dead, at both the 63- and 126-day windows.
  8. Grafting one more multiplicative rank leg onto an already-tried two-leg pair rarely decorrelates it: inserting TS_RANK(TS_MAX($high,21),63) between $earnings_per_share and TS_RANK($return,5) only reached rho 0.841 against the bare pair. This is the same failure family as the leverage/roe case above (4 rejects total this round) — a third rank leg needs to change what's measured, not just multiply into one side.
  9. TS_DELTA($earnings_per_share,63) and TS_DELTA($roe,63), each crossed with a different-window TS_RANK($dollar_volume) leg (10 vs 21), still hit rho 0.822 — the roa/roe/eps cluster stays correlated even after both legs get the same transform, so changing the volume window alone isn't a decorrelating edit here.
  10. A rejection this round shared 8 nodes with an existing archive member built on COUNT(...) — COUNT is no longer clean untried territory on this arm; check the live archive file for COUNT( before spending a proposal on it.
  11. 3 of this round's rejects were exact in-run duplicates, all earnings_per_share crossed with TS_MEAN($dollar_volume,21) or TS_MEAN($return,21) — that theme got over-sampled; spread proposals across more fields/shapes before repeating a fundamental x TS_MEAN(21) crossing.
  12. A product of two fundamental-flavored legs with no volume/price-rank leg at all (a close/book_per_share ratio times operating_margin) missed cheap_screen at |t| 0.33 — one data point, but the working product shape elsewhere this round always kept one leg as a volume/price-timing rank rather than a second fundamental.

For each proposal give a one-line economic rationale: what mechanism would make
this predict returns. "It is a momentum variant" is not a mechanism.
